The test image shows a corn leaf with a prominent dark reddish-brown elongated lesion along the midrib, containing discrete black spots/fruiting bodies embedded within it. The surrounding leaf has yellowish flecks. Key features: midrib lesion, reddish-brown color, black pycnidia-like structures.

Top candidates: Physoderma Brown Spot (midrib banding with dark sporangia), Anthracnose (dark lesions with black acervuli), Tar Spot (black raised spots).

Let me view references for top candidates sequentially.

This is a very strong match! The Physoderma Brown Spot reference shows identical features: yellowish flecks on green leaf + dark band along midrib with discrete black spots. Let me check a few more classes to confirm.

All three Physoderma Brown Spot references confirm the match. The diagnostic pattern is unmistakable:
- Green leaf with scattered yellowish flecks
- Dark reddish-brown elongated band/lesion concentrated along the midrib
- Discrete black spots (sporangia) embedded in the midrib lesion

No other class showed this combination. Anthracnose showed stalk rot, Tar Spot showed scattered black dots across the whole leaf (not midrib-banded), Gray Leaf Spot and Stewart's Disease showed completely different symptoms.
